![text](115,88,882,129) the function $\mathcal{Q}_{n_1,n_2}(k)$ which has expected density $\approx 1/N$ into roughly $N$ many harmonics $\lambda_{\chi\xi^\ell}(k)$ .

![text](134,125,549,143) Invoking Conjecture $C_1(\varepsilon)$ , we obtain for $\chi\xi^\ell \ne 1$

![formula](348,150,647,190) $$
\sum_{k \asymp NX} \Upsilon_{n_1,n_2}(k) \lambda_{\chi\xi^\ell}(k) \ll X^{1/3+2\varepsilon/3},
$$

![text](115,196,883,304) which is sufficient provided that $N < X^{1/3-2\varepsilon/3}$ . We merely require this bound on average over the complete family of $n_1, n_2 \sim N$ , $\chi \in \widehat{\mathfrak{C}(d)}$ , and $|\ell| \ll R_d$ (see Remark 7.1). It is tempting to think that this problem would be amenable to large sieve techniques but unfortunately, the cubic forms appearing in $\Upsilon_{n_1,n_2}(k)$ are entangled with $n_1, n_2$ . We mention that similar sums for a fixed discriminant and a fixed binary cubic or quartic form arise naturally in the context of Manin’s conjecture for Châtelet surfaces [37].

![text](135,304,679,322) The task is then to evaluate the main term coming from $\chi\xi^\ell = 1$

![formula](296,327,699,375) $$
\sum_{n_1,n_2 \sim N} \frac{\beta_{n_1}\beta_{n_2}}{\sqrt{n_1n_2}L(1,(\frac{4n_1n_2}{\cdot}))} \sum_{k \asymp NX} \Upsilon_{n_1,n_2}(k) \lambda_1(k).
$$

![text](115,381,882,435) It is not obvious how to make the argument unconditional and we have to assume that $\lambda_1(k)$ may be replaced by the truncated approximation $\lambda_1^\#(k,T)$ . For the divisor function along binary cubic forms Greaves has shown an asymptotic formula with a power saving [11].

![text](115,436,882,511) Using Heath-Brown’s large sieve for quadratic characters [17], on average over $n_1, n_2$ we can replace the factor $L(1,(\frac{4n_1n_2}{\cdot}))^{-1}$ by $\sum_{k \le X^\varepsilon} \frac{\mu(k)}{k}(\frac{4n_1n_2}{k})$ (see Lemma 3.5). For the truncated approximation $\lambda_1^\#(k,T) = \sum_{c \le T}(\frac{4n_1n_2}{c})$ we can evaluate the sum over $y_1, y_2$ by applying Poisson summation twice, which produces a count for cubic congruences

![formula](114,517,687,540) (1.1)

$$
\#\{(y_1, y_2) \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^2 : n_1y_2^3 \equiv n_2y_1^3 \pmod{c}\}.
$$

![text](116,548,881,581) Expanding (1.1) by cubic Dirichlet characters, the principal characters give the main term. We then need to bound error terms of the form

![formula](303,585,694,648) $$
\frac{1}{N} \sum_{c \le T} \frac{1}{c} \sum_{k \le X^\varepsilon} \frac{\mu(k)}{k} \sum_{\substack{\chi \pmod{c} \\ \chi^3 = \chi_0 \ne \chi_0}} \left| \sum_{n \sim N} \beta_n \chi(n) \left(\frac{n}{ck}\right) \right|^2.
$$

![text](116,653,839,670) This is bounded using the large sieve for sextic characters due to Baier and Young [1].

![text](115,685,882,751) 1.2.3. Type $I_2$ sums. The obtained Type I and Type II ranges would already be enough for a lower bound of the correct order of magnitude for the number of primes $p = x^2 + y^3$ . To show an asymptotic formula, we also need to consider the Type $I_2$ sums. We are able to handle these for

![formula](452,759,546,781) $$
D_2 < X^{1/4}
$$

![text](115,790,883,898) by using the spectral methods of GL(2) automorphic forms. The proof will appear in an upcoming joint work with Grimmelt [14], as an application of the *averages over orbits* introduced in [13]. To sketch the idea in the critical case $d \sim D_2$ , $m \sim n \sim \sqrt{X/D_2}$ , note that for a fixed $y$ we consider a variant of the divisor problem along a quadratic polynomial $\sum_x f(\frac{x}{A})d(x^2 + y^3)$ . Applying Poisson summation on $x$ produces the expected main term and an error term with the dual variable of length $H \approx \sqrt{D_2}$ .

![page_number](492,898,505,911) 5
